scope: Predeclared human judgments and refutable hypotheses before fresh product output. Book judgments are hypotheses, not engine facts.

cases.human_task: Explain a sound development move without inventing a defect from a small score change.
cases.hypothesis: Nc3 develops and supports e4; a meaningful preference for Bb5 requires a separate verified comparison.
falsifiers: Reference ranking or gap fails to remain stable under comparable deeper analysis.
Claimed disadvantage is also present after the alternative.

cases.human_task: Preserve known winning status of both moves; do not present a finite scalar preference as a proved defect.
cases.hypothesis: Both moves retain a tablebase win with matching reported DTZ and DTM; check and pawn-defense roles differ.
falsifiers: A claim of lost winning status contradicts stored tablebase evidence.
Equal tablebase results alone do not establish equal practical difficulty.

cases.human_task: Explain the first checking reply and lost queen-capture opportunity with their consequences.
cases.hypothesis: Moving the f1 rook permits a dangerous Qf2+ reply; the alternative captures the queen and pays the rook.
falsifiers: Qf2 is already equally effective against the alternative.
The stated follow-up can be avoided by an adequate tested defense.

cases.mainline_san: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 Nf6 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O c6 Qc2 b6 Nbd2 Bb7 e4
cases.human_task: Judge a routine developing move by whether it gives White an effective central advance and leaves Black unable to challenge the wedge in time.
cases.hypothesis: After Nbd7, e5 gains time against Nf6, closes Bb7 and leaves weaker central counterplay than Na6 followed by c5. Test each link separately.
falsifiers: e5 is legal after both moves: legality alone proves no timing difference.
A strong response after Nbd7 challenges the centre comparably.
Na6 does not improve the relevant central response or the engine rejects the book preference.

cases.human_task: Distinguish the cost of delaying d5 from the cost of moving the rook off the c-file; do not merge unproved causes.
cases.hypothesis: Immediate d5 keeps the c-file rook available for Rc4 and central/queenside pressure, while Rd8 gives White Rg1 and counterplay. Test exd5, Ne2 and Rg1 and alternative Black responses.
falsifiers: Black can recover the same pressure after Rd8 and Rg1.
A tested defense refutes the immediate d5 line.
The difference is adequately explained by a separate forcing tactic rather than timing.

cases.human_task: Explain Rhd1 as support for d5/c5 and Rhf1 as preparation for f4 without inventing superiority.
cases.hypothesis: Two useful plans exist; Rhd1 changes support of d5 so c4 can advance, but Black Nc5 can contest this plan and must not be ignored.
falsifiers: The claimed c5 plan ignores an effective Nc5 response.
A modern concrete refutation makes one plan materially worse.
Support geometry is mistaken for proof that c5 succeeds.
